questions.title: Synapsis defined: pairing along the chromosome's length
questions.subject: dev
questions.question: What does the biological term 'synapsis' specifically mean during cell division?

options.B: Pairing of homologous chromosomes at the centromere only
options.C: Alignment of non-homologous structures across the equator
options.D: Pairing of homologous chromosomes along their length

explanations.A: Incorrect. Synapsis pairs homologous chromosomes (one maternal, one paternal copy of the same chromosome), not the sister chromatids of a single already-duplicated chromosome.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Synapsis is not restricted to the centromere; the defining feature is that pairing occurs along the entire length of each homologous chromosome, not at a single point.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Synapsis specifically pairs homologous structures, not non-homologous ones, and it is not an equatorial alignment process (that describes metaphase positioning, a separate event).
explanations.D: Correct. Synapsis is the intimate pairing of homologous chromosomes along their entire length during prophase I of meiosis, mediated by the synaptonemal complex, forming the bivalent (tetrad) structure that permits crossing-over between non-sister chromatids. The paired structure formed by each homologous pair in this way is called a bivalent, or tetrad when counting all four chromatids.

questions.learning_objective: Define synapsis as the length-wise pairing of homologous chromosomes during prophase I of meiosis via the synaptonemal complex, distinct from any pairing of sister chromatids.
